relevant_findings.topic: EA-based unit of measure with SIZE BUCKETS — 3 PS keys
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior windows use the Size Bucket Method: PS_EXT_OPENING_EA.WINDOW_S (glass area < 6 SF), PS_EXT_OPENING_EA.WINDOW_M (glass area 6-15 SF), PS_EXT_OPENING_EA.WINDOW_L (glass area > 15 SF). Visual categorization during exterior walkthrough. This is fundamentally different from the door spec's single EA key — windows have 3 keys that drive 3 distinct production rate tiers based on physical size. Window type (awning, casement, double_hung, bay, bow) is an additional modifier WITHIN each size bucket.

relevant_findings.topic: Window type drives production rate dramatically within size buckets
relevant_findings.finding: Production rates per coat vary significantly by window type: Awning 0.4-0.8 hrs/coat (simplest profile), Casement 0.5-1.0 hrs/coat (single sash), Double-hung 1.0-1.5 hrs/coat (most common, two operable sashes), Bay 1.5-2.5 hrs/coat (multiple sashes + structural frame), Bow 2.0-3.0 hrs/coat (most complex profile). Window type is the primary production rate driver alongside size bucket.

relevant_findings.topic: Three cladding types with distinct prep and primer requirements
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior windows come in three cladding materials: (1) Wood sash — traditional painted wood, standard prep and primer. (2) Aluminum-clad — nonporous, slick substrate requiring scuff-sand (180-220 grit) for mechanical bonding profile + industrial-grade corrosion-inhibiting primer (e.g., Sherwin-Williams Pro-Cryl). (3) Vinyl-clad — low surface energy + high thermal sensitivity, requires PVC bonding primer (e.g., INSL-X STIX) and VinylSafe IR-reflective colors only (LRV restriction).

relevant_findings.topic: 1/16 inch glass lap creates weather seal — critical rule
relevant_findings.finding: Paint must overlap glass by exactly 1/16 inch. This encapsulates glazing putty and creates a weather-tight seal. The glass lap is not cosmetic — it is a functional moisture barrier. Without the glass lap, water infiltrates between the putty and glass, causing glazing failure, wood rot, and paint peeling around the glass perimeter. This technique requires precision brush work.

relevant_findings.topic: Sash painting sequence prevents blocking (sashes sealing shut)
relevant_findings.finding: Blocking = paint acts as adhesive, sealing operable sashes shut. Protocol: (1) Remove all window hardware, locks, lifts. (2) Free stuck windows with window zipper or utility knife. (3) Sash reversal — pull upper sash down, push lower sash up to expose top rail of upper and bottom rail of lower. (4) Paint horizontal rails first, then vertical stiles (brush with grain). (5) Glass lap at 1/16 inch. (6) Return sashes to nearly closed, leaving 1 inch gap top and bottom until dry. (7) Gently move sashes periodically during drying to prevent bonding.

relevant_findings.topic: Never-paint zones on windows — channels, weatherstripping, cords
relevant_findings.finding: Never paint: sliding channels (pulley stiles), weatherstripping, sash cords. Instead: lubricate unpainted contact points with light wax or linseed oil. Painting these components causes sash binding, weatherstrip failure, and cord degradation. These are EXCLUSION zones within the window assembly.

relevant_findings.topic: Low-E glass — liquid masking PROHIBITED
relevant_findings.finding: Do NOT use liquid masking products (e.g., Jasco Mask & Peel) on Low-E coated glass. The scoring step during removal damages the specialized Low-E coating. Use only tape-and-film masking method on Low-E glass. This is a HARD STOP decision point that must be captured at scope time.

relevant_findings.topic: Masking methods — tape/film vs liquid mask
relevant_findings.finding: Two glass masking methods: (1) Tape and film — medium-adhesion blue painter's tape for frames/glass, HDPE plastic film across glass, secondary tape line to prevent film flutter from wind. Score tape with utility knife for razor-sharp paint line. (2) Liquid masking — brush heavily over glass, cures into protective membrane, score trim line and peel post-spraying. Liquid mask is excellent for complex divided-lite windows (muntins) but PROHIBITED on Low-E glass.

relevant_findings.topic: Muntin/grille complexity — TDL vs SDL vs GBG
relevant_findings.finding: Three muntin/grille configurations affect production: (1) True Divided Lites (TDL) — actual mullion bars dividing individual glass panes, each pane must be individually masked, each muntin bar painted. Massive labor increase. (2) Simulated Divided Lites (SDL) — applied muntin bars on single glass pane, bars are painted but masking is simpler (single pane behind bars). (3) Grilles Between Glass (GBG) — grilles sandwiched between insulated glass panes, NO painting required. GBG windows are treated as single-lite for production purposes.

relevant_findings.topic: Vinyl-clad LRV restriction — VinylSafe IR-reflective ONLY
relevant_findings.finding: Dark standard paints warp vinyl frames. Vinyl-clad windows require VinylSafe IR-reflective color palettes (Sherwin-Williams VinylSafe Color Technology: 100 color options including dark colors LRV < 55). Standard paint on vinyl: LRV must be 55+ to avoid warping, buckling, and manufacturer warranty voidance. With VinylSafe IR-reflective coatings, LRV can go as low as 35-40.

relevant_findings.topic: Aluminum-clad requires corrosion-inhibiting primer
relevant_findings.finding: Aluminum-clad windows: nonporous, slick factory finish. Prep: scrape flaking finishes (if any), scuff-sand entire surface with 180-220 grit for mechanical bonding profile. Remove oxidation/chalking with TSP or detergents. Primer: industrial-grade corrosion-inhibiting primer. Topcoat: two coats flexible, high-performance exterior acrylic. This is a distinct workflow branch from wood windows.

relevant_findings.topic: Brush-only is primary for window painting — spray rarely used
relevant_findings.finding: Windows are predominantly brush-only work due to precision requirements (1/16 inch glass lap, sash painting sequence, cutting in around glass). Spray is used ONLY when windows are masked as part of a whole-house spray operation — in that case, the window frame/sash is sprayed along with the trim, but precision glass-lap work still requires brush follow-up. Roller is NOT used on window components. Application method dimension: brush (primary), spray (conditional, whole-house spray only).

relevant_findings.topic: Reglazing as conditional task — 0.27 hrs/LM additional
relevant_findings.finding: Reglazing adds 0.27 labor hours per linear meter of glazing bed. Glazing condition assessment drives the task: sound (no reglaze), minor failure (partial reglaze — remove only loose sections), widespread failure (full reglaze to all compounds). NC windows should have sound glazing — this is primarily a repaint concern. However, some NC wood windows with traditional glazing may require initial glazing sealing as part of the painting process.

relevant_findings.topic: Bay and bow window geometry — multi-sash assemblies
relevant_findings.finding: Bay windows: typically 3 sashes (center fixed, two flanking operable) plus structural frame/seat/head. Projected outward from wall plane. Bow windows: 4-5+ sashes arranged in a curved arc, more complex profile than bay. Both types have significantly higher production times due to: multiple sash units per assembly, structural frame painting, interior seat/head painting, and complex angle cuts at glass-to-frame intersections.

relevant_findings.topic: Window components — frame, sash, muntin, jamb extension, stool, apron
relevant_findings.finding: Paintable window components within this spec: (1) Frame — the fixed outer structure. (2) Sash — the movable panel holding the glass. (3) Muntin bars — dividers between glass panes (TDL and SDL only). (4) Jamb extension — interior-facing jamb visible from exterior when window is open. (5) Stool — interior horizontal ledge at window base (may be exterior-facing on some installations). (6) Apron — trim piece below the stool. EXCLUDED: exterior window casing/trim belongs to SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1 (measured via PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_WINDOW_CASING).

relevant_findings.topic: Height is a major modifier — upper story windows are always elevated work
relevant_findings.finding: Unlike doors (typically ground level), windows are frequently at 2nd and 3rd story elevations. Height modifiers from Access Staging Doctrine: ground/1-story = 1.00, 2-story = 1.15-1.25, 3-story = 1.35-1.50, 4+ story = 1.50-1.75. Window painting at height requires ladder repositioning (every 4-6 ft lateral) or pump jack platform. Pump jacks recover approximately 50% of the height penalty. Height modifier applies to ALL window painting tasks.

relevant_findings.topic: Sheen selection for exterior windows — trim-class sheen
relevant_findings.finding: Windows follow the trim sheen configuration: satin, semi-gloss, or gloss. Per Exterior_Color_Sheen_Configuration_Doctrine.md, trim sheen is a project-level selection with no locked-in default. Higher sheen provides better durability, dirt resistance, and UV fade resistance — all desirable for windows exposed to weather. Gloss requires higher prep quality as it reveals surface imperfections.

relevant_findings.topic: Glazing compound types and cure times before painting
relevant_findings.finding: Glazing materials: Sarco Dual Glaze (field use) or Sarco Multi-Glaze Type M (shop use) recommended. Avoid off-the-shelf big box putties (dry inconsistently, mildew easily). Traditional linseed oil putties must cure and skin (days to weeks via oxidation) before painting. Glazing sealing procedure: scrape bed clean, apply 50/50 boiled linseed oil/denatured alcohol to seal dried wood, back-bed glass with putty, secure with glazier's points, face-glaze and tool to smooth profile.

relevant_findings.topic: Failure modes — moisture infiltration is leading cause
relevant_findings.finding: Leading window paint failure: unpainted bottom sash edges wick water via capillary action causing rot and blistering. Missing vapor barriers allow interior humidity to migrate outward causing exterior paint peeling. Failed glazing putty allows rain to pool in wood rebate causing peeling around glass perimeter. Temperature blisters from painting in direct sunlight. Intercoat peeling from inadequate cleaning of chalky residues or waiting > 2 weeks between primer and topcoat.

relevant_findings.topic: Cross-grain cracking on historically over-painted windows
relevant_findings.finding: Cross-grain cracking occurs when combined paint film thickness from many repaint cycles loses elasticity. The cure is total paint removal to bare wood — no partial solution. This is primarily a repaint issue but relevant for NC spec awareness: NC windows start with zero film buildup, so proper DFT targets prevent future cross-grain cracking.

condition_drivers.impact: Primary production rate driver. Awning (simplest) to bow (most complex). Double-hung requires sash reversal sequence. Bay/bow are multi-sash assemblies with structural frame. Fixed windows are simple (no operable sash). Each type has distinct painting protocol and hours/coat.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION — changes both rate and workflow. Fixed windows added because they are common in NC and have the simplest workflow (no operable sash, no blocking prevention).

condition_drivers.impact: Drives primer selection, surface prep protocol, and topcoat restrictions. Wood = standard acrylic primer. Aluminum-clad = scuff-sand 180-220 grit + corrosion-inhibiting primer. Vinyl-clad = bonding primer + VinylSafe IR-reflective colors only (LRV >= 55 standard, >= 35-40 with VinylSafe).
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION — affects task structure for prep and prime phases. Vinyl-clad also constrains topcoat color selection.

condition_drivers.impact: Determines prep depth and primer requirement. Bare wood = full prime + all-edge sealing. Factory-primed = light scuff + topcoat (wood), or degloss + topcoat (aluminum/vinyl). Field-primed = direct topcoat. SS_EXT_BARE_METAL not applicable — window frames are wood, aluminum-clad, or vinyl-clad (not bare metal).
condition_drivers.notes: SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY is the dominant NC state for aluminum-clad and vinyl-clad. SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD is dominant for wood windows.

condition_drivers.impact: QT3: standard 2-coat with clean glass lap. QT4: premium materials, light sand between coats, raking light inspection. QT5: hand-sand between all coats, precision masking, DFT verification. QT2 not applicable — exterior windows are visible architectural elements.
condition_drivers.notes: QT5 is applicable to showcase homes and historic-style windows with TDL muntins.

condition_drivers.impact: Sheen is a project-level selection with no locked-in default. Windows follow trim-class sheen. Higher sheen = more durable but reveals surface imperfections. Gloss requires higher prep quality.

Brush is PRIMARY for window painting — precision required for glass lap, sash sequence, and cutting in around glass. Spray is CONDITIONAL — only when windows are part of a whole-house spray operation, and even then brush follow-up is needed for glass-lap precision. Roller is NOT a valid option for window components.
condition_drivers.notes: Brush is the dominant method. Spray adds masking labor overhead that often exceeds the spray speed advantage on small window surfaces.

condition_drivers.impact: True Divided Lites (TDL): massive labor increase — each individual pane must be masked, each muntin bar painted. Simulated Divided Lites (SDL): moderate increase — applied muntin bars painted but simpler masking (single pane). Grilles Between Glass (GBG): NO painting impact — treated as single-lite window. None: standard single-lite window.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a MODIFIER, not a configuration dimension. TDL is a major cost multiplier (+50-100% over single-lite).

condition_drivers.impact: Ground = 1.00 baseline. 2-story = 1.15-1.25 multiplier. 3-story = 1.35-1.50 multiplier. Height is a MAJOR modifier for windows — unlike doors (ground level), many windows are on upper stories. Pump jacks recover approximately 50% of height penalty.
condition_drivers.notes: Consumed from PS_EXT_META.ENUM.ACCESS_TYPE. Applied to ALL window painting tasks.

quality_differences.description: Standard exterior window. Clean and prep per cladding type. Primer per substrate state. Two finish coats with mid-grade 100% acrylic exterior trim enamel. Clean 1/16 inch glass lap. Sash painting sequence followed. Hardware removal and reinstall.

Premium exterior window. Same as QT3 plus: premium materials (SW Emerald Urethane Trim Enamel, BM Aura). Light sand between finish coats (220-grit). Raking light inspection for runs, sags, holidays. Fill minor imperfections with glazing putty. Precision glass-lap masking lines.

Supreme exterior window. Hand-sand between ALL coats (primer and finish) with 220-320 grit. DFT verification with gauge. Liquid mask for precision glass lap lines on non-Low-E glass (tape-and-film on Low-E). Muntin detail work with fine artist brushes. Final inspection with raking light at multiple angles.
quality_differences.typical_use: Historic-style homes, showcase properties, TDL muntin windows.

failure_modes.name: Moisture infiltration from unpainted sash edges
failure_modes.description: Unpainted bottom sash edges wick water via capillary action into end-grain wood. Causes rot, swelling, and paint blistering from the inside out. Bottom rail of lower sash and top rail of upper sash are most vulnerable.
failure_modes.prevention: Paint ALL sash edges including top and bottom rails. Use sash reversal technique to access hidden rail surfaces. Seal end-grain with primer before topcoat.
failure_modes.detection: Paint peeling at bottom of sash, wood swelling at rail joints, visible rot at bottom rail.

failure_modes.name: Sash blocking — paint bonds sash shut
failure_modes.description: Paint acts as adhesive between sash and frame, sealing operable sashes shut. Common on double-hung windows where upper and lower sashes contact each other and the frame channels.
failure_modes.prevention: Follow sash painting sequence: leave 1 inch gap top and bottom during drying. Gently move sashes periodically during drying. NEVER paint sliding channels (pulley stiles). Lubricate unpainted contact points with light wax.
failure_modes.detection: Sash will not open. Paint film visibly bonding sash to frame. Cracking paint at sash-frame junction when forced open.

failure_modes.name: Vinyl frame warping from dark color heat absorption
failure_modes.description: Standard dark paint (LRV < 55) absorbs excessive solar heat, causing vinyl frame material to soften, warp, and distort. Can break glass seals on insulated units.
failure_modes.prevention: HARD STOP: Vinyl-clad windows require VinylSafe IR-reflective color palette. Standard paint LRV must be 55+. With VinylSafe, LRV can go to 35-40. IR-reflective pigments reduce surface temperature 20-30 degrees F.
failure_modes.detection: Visible frame warping, glass seal failure, gaps between sash and frame.

failure_modes.name: Low-E glass coating damage from liquid masking
failure_modes.description: Liquid masking products (e.g., Jasco Mask & Peel) require scoring for removal. The scoring action scratches and damages the Low-E coating on the interior glass surface, permanently reducing the window's energy performance.
failure_modes.prevention: HARD STOP: Do NOT use liquid masking on Low-E glass. Use tape-and-film method only. Low-E status must be captured at scope time.
failure_modes.detection: Visible scratches on glass interior surface. Reduced insulating performance. Iridescent patches on glass.

failure_modes.name: Temperature blisters from painting in direct sunlight
failure_modes.description: Direct sunlight heats fresh paint causing premature surface skinning. Trapped vaporizing solvents expand into blisters under the skinned surface.
failure_modes.prevention: Follow the sun — paint in shade. Schedule elevation painting based on sun orientation (north elevations in morning, south in afternoon, etc.).
failure_modes.detection: Blisters on sun-exposed window surfaces. Blisters contain air/gas, not liquid water.

failure_modes.name: Intercoat peeling from delayed topcoat
failure_modes.description: Waiting more than 2 weeks between primer and topcoat allows primer surface to chalk and degrade, reducing intercoat adhesion. Particularly critical on exterior surfaces exposed to UV and weather.
failure_modes.prevention: Apply topcoat within 2 weeks of primer. If delay exceeds 2 weeks, light sand primer surface and clean before topcoat.
failure_modes.detection: Topcoat peeling cleanly from primer surface. No adhesion between coats.

failure_modes.name: Glazing putty failure from missing glass lap
failure_modes.description: Without the 1/16 inch glass lap, glazing putty is exposed to direct weather. Rain pools in the wood rebate between glass and putty, causing putty deterioration, water infiltration behind the glass, and wood rot in the rebate.
failure_modes.prevention: Maintain 1/16 inch glass lap on all glazed windows. Paint must encapsulate the putty-to-glass junction.
failure_modes.detection: Paint peeling around glass perimeter. Visible putty cracking or separation from glass. Water staining below window.

primer_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Latex Exterior Primer
primer_systems.description: Standard exterior primer for bare wood window frames and sashes. Remains flexible long-term, good tannin blocking for most wood species. Penetrates into wood grain for adhesion.
primer_systems.notes: Primary primer for wood windows. For tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood), supplement with alkyd spot-prime at knots.

primer_systems.name: Alkyd/Shellac Spot Primer
primer_systems.description: Spot-applied to visible wood knots on tannin-rich species before full acrylic primer coat. Superior tannin stain blocking prevents bleed-through on cedar, redwood, and fir window components.
primer_systems.notes: Knot spot-priming only — not full surface. Required for tannin-rich species.

primer_systems.name: Corrosion-Inhibiting Primer for Aluminum-Clad
primer_systems.description: Industrial-grade corrosion-inhibiting primer (e.g., Sherwin-Williams Pro-Cryl). Provides adhesion to scuff-sanded aluminum cladding and corrosion protection. Must be applied over mechanical bonding profile created by 180-220 grit sanding.
primer_systems.notes: Mandatory for aluminum-clad windows. Surface must be scuff-sanded first. Remove all oxidation/chalking with TSP before priming.

primer_systems.name: PVC Bonding Primer for Vinyl-Clad
primer_systems.description: Specialized PVC bonding primer (e.g., INSL-X STIX). Grips the low-energy vinyl surface and provides adhesion bridge for topcoat. Critical for vinyl substrate — standard primers will not bond.
primer_systems.notes: Mandatory for vinyl-clad windows. Bonding primer must be recoated within 1 week or it becomes brittle and loses flexibility for topcoat bond.

topcoat_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Latex Exterior Trim Enamel
topcoat_systems.description: Standard exterior window finish. Hard enamel for UV resistance and durability on weather-exposed surfaces. Flexible enough for thermal expansion/contraction on all cladding types.
topcoat_systems.notes: QT3: mid-grade (SW SuperPaint Exterior, BM Regal Select). QT4: premium (SW Emerald Urethane Trim Enamel, BM Aura). Must be 100% acrylic for flexibility on exterior surfaces.

topcoat_systems.name: VinylSafe IR-Reflective Exterior Enamel
topcoat_systems.description: IR-reflective coating with Complex Inorganic Color Pigments (CICPs). Required for vinyl-clad windows when color LRV < 55. Allows dark visual colors without excessive heat absorption. Drops surface temperature 20-30 degrees F.
topcoat_systems.notes: MANDATORY for vinyl-clad windows with color LRV < 55. Material cost premium over standard acrylic enamel. SW VinylSafe Color Technology palette (100 colors).

topcoat_systems.name: Premium Urethane-Modified Acrylic Trim Enamel
topcoat_systems.description: Highest-performance exterior trim enamel for QT5 window work. Urethane-modified for maximum hardness, gloss retention, and UV resistance. Self-leveling for brush-mark-free finish on detailed muntin work.
topcoat_systems.notes: QT5 only. SW Emerald Urethane Trim Enamel or equivalent. Self-leveling properties critical for muntin detail work.

notes_for_materials_manager: Three cladding types require three distinct primer paths: wood = acrylic exterior primer, aluminum-clad = corrosion-inhibiting primer, vinyl-clad = PVC bonding primer.
Vinyl-clad windows: VinylSafe IR-reflective topcoat MANDATORY when color LRV < 55. Standard paint LRV must be 55+ without VinylSafe. This is a HARD STOP material constraint.
Bonding primer on vinyl: must be recoated within 1 week or it dries brittle — loses topcoat adhesion. Schedule accordingly.
Coverage rate for window surfaces is lower than siding/trim due to small surfaces and high cut-in ratio. Estimate 250-350 SF/gal effective coverage.
Masking materials: HDPE static-cling film for glass, pre-taped poly for trim protection. Liquid mask for TDL muntin windows (non-Low-E glass ONLY).
Low-E glass: PROHIBIT liquid masking products. Use tape-and-film method only. Flag Low-E status in material list.
Glazing putty: Sarco Dual Glaze for field use. Avoid big-box putties. Include whiting/pumice powder for oily residue cleanup on glass.
Tannin-rich wood species (cedar, redwood, fir): include alkyd spot primer for knot treatment in addition to full-surface acrylic primer.
Spray tip for windows (whole-house spray): 211 or 311 (0.011-0.013 inch orifice) for precision on small surfaces. 200-mesh red filter.
Sash lubricant: light wax or linseed oil for unpainted sliding channels — include in consumable list.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Module structure: setup → protect/mask_glass → hardware_remove → clean → prep_per_cladding → prime → apply_coat_1 → sand_between (QT4/QT5) → apply_coat_2 → glass_lap_touch → hardware_reinstall → cleanup → teardown.

SASH PAINTING SEQUENCE IS CRITICAL (double-hung): sash reversal → paint rails first → stiles → glass lap → drying posture (1 inch gap) → periodic movement during drying. This is a distinct SOP module for double-hung windows.
Glass lap: 1/16 inch overlap onto glass is MANDATORY — creates weather seal. Must be specified in SOP procedure steps.
NEVER PAINT: sliding channels (pulley stiles), weatherstripping, sash cords. Lubricate with wax or linseed oil instead.
Aluminum-clad prep: scuff-sand entire surface 180-220 grit → TSP/detergent wash → dry → corrosion-inhibiting primer. Distinct module from wood prep.
Vinyl-clad prep: clean with TSP substitute → PVC bonding primer. No sanding needed — primer provides adhesion.
Low-E glass decision point: IF Low-E = true THEN mask with tape-and-film ONLY. IF Low-E = false AND muntins = TDL THEN liquid mask is permitted.
Bay/bow window SOP: treat as multi-sash assembly. Paint each sash unit individually following single-window SOP, then paint structural frame and seat/head.
Hardware removal: locks, lifts, sash pulls. Bag and label per window. Reinstall after final coat is fully dry.
Between-coat sanding: QT4 with 220-grit. QT5 with 220-320 grit and raking light inspection between each coat.
Brush sequence for all windows: horizontal rails first, then vertical stiles. Brush with the grain direction.
Spray operation (whole-house context): mask glass with HDPE static-cling film + tape → spray frame/sash with trim → remove masking → brush glass-lap line if needed.
Reglazing (conditional): scrape bed → linseed oil/alcohol seal → back-bed glass → glazier points → face-glaze → tool → cure before painting.
notes_for_estimation_engineer: This is an EA-BASED spec with SIZE BUCKETS. Three PS keys: PS_EXT_OPENING_EA.WINDOW_S, WINDOW_M, WINDOW_L. Each size bucket has distinct base rates.
Production rates by window type (hrs/EA per coat): awning 0.4-0.8, casement 0.5-1.0, double_hung 1.0-1.5, bay 1.5-2.5, bow 2.0-3.0. Fixed windows: estimate 0.3-0.6 (no operable sash).
Size bucket calibration: small windows cluster toward low end of type range, large toward high end. Medium is the calibration baseline.

Coat system: 1 primer + 2 finish coats standard for all tiers on bare wood and aluminum-clad. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY may skip prime (aluminum/vinyl — factory primer adequate). SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips prime.
HEIGHT MODIFIER IS CRITICAL for windows — apply to ALL tasks. Ground = 1.00, 2-story = 1.20 (midpoint), 3-story = 1.43 (midpoint). Height is consumed from PS_EXT_META.ENUM.ACCESS_TYPE.
Muntin modifier: none/GBG = 1.00, SDL = 1.25 (applied bars to paint), TDL = 1.50-2.00 (individual pane masking + muntin painting). TDL is a major cost multiplier.
Reglazing (conditional, wood only): +0.27 hrs per linear meter of glazing bed. Primarily a repaint task — NC windows should have sound glazing.
Glass masking: standard single-lite = 0.08-0.12 hrs/EA. TDL multi-lite = 0.20-0.50 hrs/EA depending on lite count. Bay/bow = per-sash masking.
Hardware removal/reinstall: 0.10-0.20 hrs/EA per window (locks, lifts, pulls). Simpler than door hardware.
Application method: brush is primary. No roller option. Spray only in whole-house spray context and adds masking labor that typically exceeds spray speed advantage on individual windows.
Cladding prep modifier: wood = 1.00 (baseline), aluminum_clad = 1.15 (scuff-sand labor), vinyl_clad = 0.90 (clean only, no sanding).
Environmental conditions EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers — SOP concerns only.
Bay/bow windows: treated as a single EA but rates are 2-5x higher than standard windows. Do NOT count individual sashes within bay/bow as separate EA.
Window casing (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_WINDOW_CASING) belongs to SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1 — do NOT include casing painting in this spec's rates.

assumptions.value: New construction exterior window painting — wood sash, aluminum-clad, and vinyl-clad frames. Covers frame, sash, muntin bars (TDL/SDL), jamb extension, stool, apron. Does NOT include exterior window casing/trim (covered by SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1) or interior window surfaces (covered by SF_WINDOW_INT_NC_v1).
assumptions.note: Clear scope boundary at the casing. This spec paints the window unit itself. Casing is measured separately via PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_WINDOW_CASING and painted by the trim spec.

assumptions.value: QT2 not applicable to exterior windows
assumptions.note: Exterior windows are visible architectural elements. QT3 is the minimum standard for NC residential.

assumptions.value: Repaint substrate states excluded from this NC spec
assumptions.source: User brief — 'New construction exterior window painting'
assumptions.note: Repaint adds significant labor (failed paint removal, reglazing, cross-grain cracking remediation). Requires separate spec with fundamentally different prep modules.

assumptions.value: Reglazing is rare in NC but included as conditional task for wood windows with traditional glazing
assumptions.note: Most NC windows arrive with factory-sealed IGU (insulated glass units) and do not require glazing. Traditional glazed windows (rare in NC) may require initial glazing seal before painting.

assumptions.value: Brush is primary. Spray is conditional (whole-house spray context). No roller option.
assumptions.note: Windows require precision brush work for glass lap and sash sequence. Spray adds masking overhead that rarely justifies speed advantage on individual windows.

assumptions.value: SS_EXT_BARE_METAL is not applicable to windows
assumptions.source: User brief — cladding types are wood, aluminum-clad, vinyl-clad
assumptions.note: Unlike doors, window cladding is never bare metal. Aluminum-clad arrives with factory finish that requires scuff-sand and primer. Vinyl-clad has no metal exposed. Wood is the only bare substrate possibility.

assumptions.value: Bay and bow windows are counted as 1 EA each in the large (L) size bucket, with higher per-EA production rates
assumptions.source: User brief production rates; PaintScope Size Bucket Method
assumptions.note: Doctrine does not explicitly state how bay/bow windows map to size buckets. They always have glass area > 15 SF so they fall in WINDOW_L. The window_type modifier (bay/bow) then drives the elevated production rate within the L bucket. Confirm with Eric.

uncertainties.detail: Bay and bow windows always fall into WINDOW_L (glass area > 15 SF). However, a bay window with three 4 SF panes = 12 SF total glass might be WINDOW_M by the simple glass area rule. Should bay/bow windows always be forced into WINDOW_L regardless of glass area, or should they follow the standard size bucket rules?
uncertainties.recommendation: Force bay/bow windows into WINDOW_L size bucket regardless of measured glass area. Their complexity and multi-sash geometry makes WINDOW_M rates inadequate. Alternatively, create a dedicated size bucket PS_EXT_OPENING_EA.WINDOW_BAY and PS_EXT_OPENING_EA.WINDOW_BOW.

uncertainties.detail: The stool (interior horizontal ledge) and apron (trim piece below stool) are partially interior-facing even though they are components of the window assembly. Should stool and apron painting belong to this exterior window spec, the interior window spec, or the trim spec?
uncertainties.recommendation: Include stool and apron in this spec when they are accessible from the exterior during window painting. Their painting is naturally combined with frame/sash work. Interior-only stool/apron belongs to SF_WINDOW_INT_NC_v1.

uncertainties.topic: NC production rate confidence for non-double-hung types
uncertainties.detail: Doctrine provides production rates for all window types but does not specify whether these are NC or repaint rates. The rates (awning 0.4-0.8, casement 0.5-1.0, double_hung 1.0-1.5, bay 1.5-2.5, bow 2.0-3.0) appear to be general rates. NC rates should be at the low end of these ranges (no scraping, no reglazing, no failed paint removal).
uncertainties.recommendation: Use the low-to-mid range for NC rates. Flag for field calibration. NC windows with factory primer have minimal prep — bias toward lower end.

uncertainties.topic: Fixed window type not in doctrine production rates
uncertainties.detail: The doctrine lists awning, casement, double_hung, bay, and bow but does not separately list fixed (non-operable) windows. Fixed windows should be simpler than awning (no operable sash, no blocking prevention). Estimated at 0.3-0.6 hrs/coat.
uncertainties.recommendation: Add fixed window type at 0.3-0.6 hrs/coat. Simpler than awning — no sash hardware, no blocking sequence, frame painting only.

uncertainties.detail: TDL muntin modifier estimated at 1.50-2.00x but actual multiplier depends on lite count. A 6-over-6 double-hung (12 individual panes) requires dramatically more masking than a 2-over-2 (4 panes). Per-lite time estimate needed for accurate calibration.
uncertainties.recommendation: Use lite count as sub-modifier within TDL: base TDL modifier = 1.50, add +0.10 per lite above 4. Alternatively, capture total lite count as a PaintScope meta key.

zones.notes: Glass panes in window assembly. HDPE static-cling masking film for standard single-lite. Tape-and-film for all Low-E glass. Liquid mask permitted for TDL muntin windows (non-Low-E ONLY). Masking time varies dramatically: single-lite 0.08-0.12 hrs/EA vs TDL multi-lite 0.20-0.50 hrs/EA.

Window locks, lifts, sash pulls. Remove before painting, bag and label per window. Reinstall after final coat is dry. Fixed windows have no operable hardware. No separate PaintScope key — counted per window EA.
Weatherstripping on operable sashes. NEVER PAINT weatherstripping. Remove friction-fit stripping or protect with deep tape. Fixed windows have no weatherstripping. No separate PaintScope key.

Exterior window sill below the frame. Protect from drips during window painting if sill is already finished. If sill is being painted in this cycle, no protection needed. Sill painting uses PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.SILL key.
Protect finished casing from window painting drips/overspray. Casing belongs to SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1. If casing is unfinished, no protection needed. Minimal masking — tape at casing-to-frame junction.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_mask when application_method = spray
zones.notes: Protect finished siding adjacent to window from brush drips or spray overspray. Siding protection is typically handled by the siding spec's whole-house spray masking protocol. Minimal concern for brush-applied window painting.

protection_zones_analysis.cross_spec_protection_note: Window glass masking during whole-house spray operations is the SIDING or TRIM spec's protection responsibility, not this spec's. This spec's glass masking is for when the WINDOW ITSELF is being painted and glass needs protection from frame/sash paint.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Window casing trim surrounds the window opening. May be same or different color from window frame. Casing is painted by SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1 (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_WINDOW_CASING). Clean edge at frame-to-casing junction.
Glass panes. 1/16 inch glass lap required — paint overlaps onto glass for weather seal. Precision brush work. Masking protects the rest of the glass surface.

Exterior window sill below the frame. Often painted same color/sheen as window frame. Sill is measured via PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.SILL. May be included in this spec or trim spec depending on scope definition.
Siding terminates at window casing. No direct adjacency between window frame and siding — casing intervenes.
Interior window surfaces (stool, apron, interior jamb). Painted by SF_WINDOW_INT_NC_v1. Scope boundary at the window frame-to-jamb junction.

adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Window frame has precision adjacency to glass (1/16 inch glass lap) — the most exacting edge work in exterior painting. Casing provides natural separation from siding. Interior surfaces belong to the interior window spec.

affected_conditions.notes: HEIGHT IS A MAJOR MODIFIER for windows. Unlike doors (ground level), many windows are on upper stories. Ladder = 2-story windows. Scaffold = 3-story or complex access. Pump jacks recover approximately 50% of height penalty vs ladders.

excluded_conditions.rationale: Environmental conditions are unpredictable at bid time. They are SOP/process concerns, not estimatable. Per sibling exterior spec pattern.

excluded.reason: Unpredictable at bid time. Windows are brush-applied so wind is less impactful than for spray operations.
Varies by time of day and elevation orientation. Schedule painting for shade hours.
Weather-dependent. Not predictable at bid time.
Affects drying but not production rate. SOP concern — follow the sun.

valid_input_states.rationale: NC exterior windows arrive in one of these three states. Wood windows may be bare or factory-primed. Aluminum-clad and vinyl-clad windows arrive with factory finish (SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY). Field-primed means primer already applied on-site. SS_EXT_BARE_METAL is not applicable — window cladding is never bare metal.

output_state.rationale: Output state is the painted finish. Varies by project sheen selection (satin, semi-gloss, gloss). Semi-gloss is the most common for exterior windows.

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: Protect finished casing from window painting drips. If casing is unfinished, no protection needed — it will be painted later.
Glass is ALWAYS masked during window painting. 1/16 inch glass lap applied, rest of glass fully protected.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Raw uncoated wood window frame/sash — no primer, no stain, no finish.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Light sand to remove mill glaze (120-150 grit). Fill defects with exterior wood filler. Clean. Spot-prime knots on tannin-rich species. Seal end-grain on all sash edges.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: 100% acrylic latex exterior primer (SYS_PRIMER_ACRYLIC_EXT). Alkyd spot-prime for tannin-rich species knots (SYS_PRIMER_ALKYD_SPOT).
exterior_substrate_states.notes: All sash edges must be primed and painted — unpainted edges wick moisture. Bottom rail of lower sash is the most critical moisture entry point.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Factory-applied primer or finish on window frame/sash. Applicable to all three cladding types.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Wood: light scuff (220-grit), clean. Aluminum-clad: scuff-sand entire surface (180-220 grit) for mechanical bonding, TSP wash. Vinyl-clad: clean with TSP substitute.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Wood: none — factory primer adequate if sound. Aluminum-clad: corrosion-inhibiting primer (SYS_PRIMER_CORROSION_INHIBIT) REQUIRED even over factory finish. Vinyl-clad: PVC bonding primer (SYS_PRIMER_BONDING_PVC) REQUIRED even over factory finish.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Dominant NC state for aluminum-clad and vinyl-clad. For these two cladding types, field prime over factory finish is mandatory (unlike steel doors where factory primer is adequate base). The factory finish on clad windows is typically anodized/powder-coated and requires adhesion promotion.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Field-applied exterior primer — ready for topcoat.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Light dust-off. Minimal prep — surface is paint-ready.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Occurs when prime and finish are split across mobilizations. Direct topcoat application.

exterior_access_type_analysis.treatment: Major modifier — windows are frequently at elevated positions.

scenarios.notes: First-floor windows at ground level. Baseline rate. Common for ranch-style homes.
Second-story windows. Extension ladder required. Frequent repositioning (every 4-6 ft lateral). Significant productivity loss.
Third-story windows or extended upper-story work. Pump jacks or sectional scaffold. Recovers ~50% of height penalty vs ladders.

exterior_environmental_constraints.note: Environmental constraints documented for SOP reference only — EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers.

sop_reference_only.go_threshold: < 10 mph for spray operations. Brush application is wind-tolerant.
sop_reference_only.note: Windows are primarily brush-applied so wind is less impactful than for siding spray.
Follow the sun — paint in shade. Windows on south/west elevations get very hot in afternoon sun.

sop_reference_only.rule: Surface temp must be >= 5 degrees F above dew point
sop_reference_only.note: Morning condensation on glass can run onto fresh paint on frame. Wait for glass to dry before painting adjacent frame.

sop_reference_only.rule: Maximum 14 days between primer and topcoat
sop_reference_only.note: Beyond 14 days: primer chalks and degrades, requiring re-sanding before topcoat.

sop_reference_only.rule: Traditional linseed oil putty must skin and cure before painting (days to weeks)
sop_reference_only.note: NC windows with IGU (insulated glass units) do not have traditional glazing — this is primarily a repaint/restoration concern.

awning_brush.notes: Simplest window profile. Single sash, top-hinged, limited glass area. Low end = small (S), high end = medium (M).

casement_brush.notes: Single side-hinged sash. More sash perimeter than awning. Low end = small (S), high end = medium (M).

double_hung_brush.notes: Most common residential window. Two operable sashes requiring reversal sequence. Includes blocking prevention protocol. Low end = medium (M), high end = large (L).

fixed_brush.notes: Non-operable window. Frame painting only — no sash hardware, no blocking sequence. Simplest of all types. Inferred from simpler-than-awning logic.

bay_brush.notes: Multi-sash assembly (typically 3 sashes). Includes structural frame, seat, head. Always WINDOW_L size bucket.

bow_brush.notes: Multi-sash curved assembly (4-5+ sashes). Most complex profile. Always WINDOW_L size bucket.

glass_masking_single_lite.notes: Per window — single glass pane masking with HDPE static-cling film + tape.

glass_masking_tdl.notes: Per window — TDL multi-lite masking. Time varies with lite count. Liquid mask option (non-Low-E) speeds process.

hardware_remove_reinstall.notes: Per window. Locks, lifts, sash pulls. Simpler than door hardware.

weatherstrip_protect.notes: Per operable window. Pull friction-fit stripping or deep tape.

prep_wood_bare.notes: Sand mill glaze, fill defects, spot-prime knots. Varies by window size and type.

prep_aluminum_clad.notes: Scuff-sand entire surface 180-220 grit + TSP wash. More labor than wood prep due to sanding requirement.

prep_vinyl_clad.notes: TSP substitute wash only. No sanding. Fastest prep of the three cladding types.

reglazing_conditional.notes: Additional labor per linear meter of glazing bed. Conditional — only for wood windows with traditional glazing requiring repair. Rare in NC.

key_decisions.topic: EA-based with SIZE BUCKETS — 3 PS keys
key_decisions.decision: This spec uses three PS keys: PS_EXT_OPENING_EA.WINDOW_S, WINDOW_M, WINDOW_L. Each size bucket has distinct production rates. Window type is a modifier WITHIN each size bucket.
key_decisions.rationale: PaintScope Exterior Key Catalog defines the Size Bucket Method for windows. Visual categorization by glass area: small < 6 SF, medium 6-15 SF, large > 15 SF. This is fundamentally different from the door spec (single PS key) and provides more accurate estimation by separating size classes.

key_decisions.decision: Combined (full phase_scope). Prime and finish phases have unique task keys within the single spec.
key_decisions.rationale: NC exterior windows are a single-mobilization scope — same crew primes and paints. Each phase (prime, finish) has its own task IDs and module IDs. Matches sibling exterior spec pattern (SF_DOOR_EXT_NC_v1).

key_decisions.decision: cladding_type (wood/aluminum_clad/vinyl_clad) is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION — changes task structure, primer system, and topcoat restrictions.
key_decisions.rationale: Each cladding requires fundamentally different prep, primer, and potentially topcoat. Aluminum-clad requires corrosion-inhibiting primer. Vinyl-clad requires bonding primer and VinylSafe IR-reflective topcoat for dark colors. These are workflow branches, not rate modifiers.

key_decisions.decision: window_type (awning/casement/double_hung/fixed/bay/bow) is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION — changes rate and SOP workflow.
key_decisions.rationale: Double-hung requires sash reversal and blocking prevention (unique SOP module). Bay/bow are multi-sash assemblies with structural frame work. Fixed windows skip all operable-sash tasks. Rates are non-overlapping across types. This is a task-structure and rate branch.

key_decisions.decision: QT2 is NOT applicable to exterior windows.
key_decisions.rationale: Exterior windows are visible architectural elements. QT3 is the minimum standard for NC residential. No economy tier.

key_decisions.decision: QT5 IS applicable to exterior windows.
key_decisions.rationale: Historic-style windows with TDL muntins, showcase properties, and architect-specified window packages justify QT5 — hand-sand between all coats, precision masking, DFT verification.

key_decisions.topic: Application method — brush primary, no roller
key_decisions.decision: Brush is primary. Spray is conditional (whole-house spray context). Roller is NOT a valid option.
key_decisions.rationale: Windows require precision brush work: 1/16 inch glass lap, sash painting sequence, cutting in around glass. Spray adds masking overhead. Roller is inappropriate for window components (surface too small, precision too high).

key_decisions.decision: Window casing painting belongs to SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1, NOT this spec.
key_decisions.rationale: Per PaintScope Exterior Key Catalog: PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_WINDOW_CASING is a trim key. Casing is measured in LF and painted by the trim spec. This spec covers the window unit itself (frame, sash, muntin, jamb extension, stool, apron).

key_decisions.topic: Low-E glass as hard stop for liquid masking
key_decisions.decision: Low-E glass PROHIBITS liquid masking. Tape-and-film method only.
key_decisions.rationale: Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md §8: liquid masking scoring damages Low-E coating. This is a binary decision captured at scope time. Violation causes permanent window performance degradation.

key_decisions.decision: Vinyl-clad windows require VinylSafe IR-reflective topcoat when color LRV < 55.
key_decisions.rationale: Per Exterior_Color_Sheen_Configuration_Doctrine.md: standard dark paint warps vinyl. VinylSafe IR-reflective allows LRV down to 35-40. This is a HARD STOP for vinyl-clad windows — failure causes frame warping and seal failure.

key_decisions.decision: EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers. Per sibling exterior spec pattern.
key_decisions.rationale: Environmental conditions are unpredictable at bid time. They belong in SOP procedure notes, not production rate modifiers.

key_decisions.decision: Height modifier is a MAJOR MODIFIER applied to all tasks. Consumed from PS_EXT_META.ENUM.ACCESS_TYPE.
key_decisions.rationale: Unlike doors (ground level), windows are frequently elevated. Height modifier values: ground 1.00, ladder 1.20, scaffold 1.43. This is the most impactful site condition modifier for windows.

key_decisions.topic: Muntin type as modifier (not configuration dimension)
key_decisions.decision: Muntin type (none/tdl/sdl/gbg) is a MODIFIER, not a configuration dimension.
key_decisions.rationale: Muntin type affects production rate and masking labor but does not fundamentally change the task structure. TDL adds masking time and muntin painting time. SDL adds bar painting time. GBG has no impact (no painting needed). These are rate multipliers within the existing task structure.

key_decisions.decision: 1 primer + 2 finish coats standard for bare wood and aluminum-clad. Vinyl-clad: 1 bonding primer + 2 finish coats. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips prime. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY: wood skips prime, aluminum-clad and vinyl-clad still require field prime (corrosion-inhibiting or bonding primer).
key_decisions.rationale: Aluminum-clad and vinyl-clad ALWAYS require field primer even over factory finish because the factory finish (anodized/powder-coat) requires adhesion promotion. Wood factory primer is an adequate base for topcoat.

key_decisions.decision: SS_EXT_BARE_METAL is not included in this spec's valid substrate states.
key_decisions.rationale: Window cladding is wood, aluminum-clad (factory-finished), or vinyl-clad (factory-finished). Bare metal does not occur in NC window context. The aluminum-clad state uses SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY (the factory anodized/powder-coat finish).

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Window type is the primary production rate driver. Must be captured per window during scope to route to correct production rate tier. Cannot be inferred from size bucket alone. A large casement and a large double-hung have very different production times.
proposed_new_keys.alternative: Could capture as a per-window attribute within the PaintScope scope record rather than a global ENUM. However, a project typically has a dominant window type — capture dominant type with per-window override.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Cladding type drives primer system, prep protocol, and topcoat restrictions. Must be captured to route to correct workflow branch. A project typically has uniform cladding but mixed cladding is possible.
proposed_new_keys.alternative: Could be a project-level default with per-window override.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Muntin type dramatically affects masking labor and painting time. TDL is a 1.5-2.0x multiplier. Must be captured to route to correct masking method and production rate modifier.
proposed_new_keys.alternative: Could be captured as a per-window attribute. Most NC homes have uniform muntin type across all windows.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Low-E glass status is a HARD STOP for liquid masking. Must be captured at scope time. Most NC windows have Low-E glass. This flag gates the masking method decision.
proposed_new_keys.alternative: Could assume true for all NC windows (most have Low-E) and only flag non-Low-E as the exception.
